<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="סיון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918734_theRebbe_176" batchId="meluket-_D7_A1_D7_99_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918734_theRebbe_176__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The root of the particular is higher than the general, as seen in Chochmah and Binah, and likewise in speech and in teaching, where the particularization reveals new depth.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">The explanation is,</t>
    <t s="1">that the root of the particular is higher than the general.</t>
    <t s="2">And like Chochmah and Binah,</t>
    <t s="3">for although Chochmah is the general from which all the particulars of Binah are drawn,</t>
    <t s="4">nevertheless, from this very aspect,</t>
    <t s="5">the root of Binah is higher than the root of Chochmah.</t>
    <t s="6">Therefore,</t>
    <t s="7">through contemplation of the particulars of Binah, there are added</t>
    <t s="8">(sometimes)</t>
    <t s="9">new matters that were not in the point of Chochmah.</t>
    <t s="10">And similarly with speech,</t>
    <t s="11">that when the intellect is drawn into speech, there are produced in it many more particulars, even more than the particulars of Binah</t>
    <t s="12">(even after Binah is clothed in thought,</t>
    <t s="13">for what one thinks in a single thought, in speech it takes a span of time),</t>
    <t s="14">for the root of speech is higher even than the root of Binah,</t>
    <t s="15">therefore when one learns the intellect through speech,</t>
    <t s="16">new matters are generated for him that were not initially in thought,</t>
    <t s="17">even in the comprehension of Binah.</t>
    <t s="18">And similarly with the influence of intellect from a teacher to a student,</t>
    <t s="19">that through the intellect being particularized into many particulars</t>
    <t s="20">[and especially through the influence to a young student,</t>
    <t s="21">for the more the influence is to a younger student,</t>
    <t s="22">the more one must particularize the intellect into many particulars],</t>
    <t s="23">behold through this there is added to the teacher a new depth that was not with him before the influence,</t>
    <t s="24">as the saying,</t>
    <t s="25">"And from my students more than all of them."</t>
    <t s="26">And especially when the student raises difficulties on the intellect,</t>
    <t s="27">that in order to answer and remove the difficulty,</t>
    <t s="28">a new depth is awakened within him.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The analogy is understood above regarding the Ten Utterances, where through service in the world created by them, one reaches higher than the general aspect of the one utterance, even to the essence of the light.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the analogy from this will be understood above regarding the matter of the Ten Utterances,</t>
    <t s="1">for although the Ten Utterances are the particulars of the one utterance,</t>
    <t s="2">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="3">from this very aspect,</t>
    <t s="4">since the root of the particular is higher than the general,</t>
    <t s="5">therefore through the service in the world that was created with Ten Utterances</t>
    <t s="6">[and especially that from this aspect that the world was created with Ten Utterances there is the possibility to choose also the opposite</t>
    <t s="7">(as above in section 6),</t>
    <t s="8">in the likeness of the difficulties that contradict the intellect],</t>
    <t s="9">one reaches higher than the aspect of the general of the world of the one utterance,</t>
    <t s="10">and furthermore,</t>
    <t s="11">that one reaches also the essence of the light,</t>
    <t s="12">which is above even the light</t>
    <t s="13">(the spreading forth of the light)</t>
    <t s="14">in which was the elevation of the will to the worlds.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Similarly with the drawing down of Torah, through its particularization from the general, the particulars of the Oral Torah contain the light of the general of the Written Torah, up to the one utterance.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And now similarly is it also regarding the drawing down of Torah,</t>
    <t s="2">that through its being drawn down initially in the aspect of a general and then particularized into particulars,</t>
    <t s="3">behold the particulars are</t>
    <t s="4">(not a matter in themselves,</t>
    <t s="5">but rather)</t>
    <t s="6">particulars that emanate from the general,</t>
    <t s="7">and through this there is the power that also in the particulars of the Oral Torah,</t>
    <t s="8">and even to everything that a veteran student will innovate in the future,</t>
    <t s="9">there will be a revelation of the light of the general of the Written Torah,</t>
    <t s="10">and even to the general of the Ten Commandments</t>
    <t s="11">(that the study of every particular in Torah will be with awe and fear and trembling and sweat as it was at the time of the utterance of the Ten Commandments),</t>
    <t s="12">and even to the general of the one utterance in which all the Ten Commandments were included.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
